steps.title: Business problem
steps.tip: Get a worked example signed off (cured 12 July, missed 27 July = re-delinquent) before writing any code.
steps.tip_ar: اعتمد مثالًا محلولًا (انتظم 12 يوليو وتعثّر 27 يوليو = تكرار تعثّر) قبل كتابة أي كود.

blocks.text: The problem, in the business user's words

segs.t: We run personal finance, auto finance, credit cards and home finance (Murabaha, Tawarruq and Ijara) through branches in Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam, Makkah, Madinah, Khobar, Abha and Tabuk. When a customer misses an installment, collections chase them until they pay and become current again. We count that as a win.

The trouble is that many of these "cured" customers miss again within a month. We call this 30-day re-delinquency. Each repeat pushes up expected credit losses under IFRS 9, so provisions go up. It also sends the same customers back to the same collectors, which wastes team capacity.

SAMA reviews our arrears and provisioning. A high repeat rate in one product or region draws questions we cannot answer today, because the data sits in the core banking system and in spreadsheets that do not agree.

blocks.text: Business goals locked with the business user

segs.t: Identify 30-day re-delinquencies: a new missed installment whose due date falls 0–30 days after the same customer cured the previous delinquency on the same product.
Highlight the products and customer segments (Retail / Affluent / Private, Saudi / Expat) that drive most of them.
Compare performance across branches, relationship managers and regions.

blocks.text: Actions

segs.t: Write the three goals and the re-delinquency definition into the project README.
Get sign-off from the head of collections on the 30-day window and on "same customer + same product".
Agree the reporting currency (SAR) and calendar (Gregorian, with an optional Hijri column).
the business user confirms the definition with a worked example: cured on 12 July, missed again on 27 July = 15 days = re-delinquent.

steps.goal: Agree in writing what the business wants before any resource is built.

segs.t: In production, the core banking system feeds a nightly Azure Data Factory extract into ADLS staging. This guide replaces those two boxes by uploading CSV files, so everything from staging onwards is real.

segs.t: Source: in a real bank, Temenos T24 or Infosys Finacle holds customers, facilities and installment schedules. Azure Data Factory runs a nightly copy (through a self-hosted integration runtime if the core system is on-premises) and writes one CSV per entity to
Simulation: in Step 8 you upload four CSV files to the same folders. Bronze cannot tell the difference.
Layers, all in Unity Catalog catalog
Bronze: raw copy of each feed, append only.
Silver: de-duplicated, typed, masked dims and one wide fact, kept current with MERGE.
Gold: the 30-day flag per event and the branch × product KPI table.
Orchestration and delivery: a Lakeflow Job on serverless runs the notebooks (Step 12). An Asset Bundle and GitHub Actions deploy it to dev and prod (Steps 13–14).
Consumers: a Genie space and an AI/BI dashboard, both opened from Databricks One (Steps 15–16).

steps.tip: Auto Loader remembers what it has read: rerunning never reloads old files.

segs.t: In the Git folder, Create → Folder →

blocks.text:
# Bronze: customers feed -> banking.bronze.cbs_customer
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, current_timestamp

entity       = "customers"          # staging folder name
table        = "cbs_customer"   # <source>_<entity>
schema_hints = "customer_id STRING, national_id_or_iqama STRING"

base        = "abfss://data@<storage-account>.dfs.core.windows.net"
source_path = f"{base}/staging/{entity}/"
schema_path = f"{base}/schemas/bronze/{table}/"
checkpoint  = f"{base}/checkpoints/bronze/{table}/"
target      = f"banking.bronze.{table}"

df = (
    spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles")
    .option("cloudFiles.format", "csv")
    .option("header", "true")
    .option("cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes", "true")
    .option("cloudFiles.schemaHints", schema_hints)
    .option("cloudFiles.maxFilesPerTrigger", 1)
    .option("cloudFiles.schemaLocation", schema_path)
    .load(source_path)
    .drop("_rescued_data")
    .withColumn("source_file", col("_metadata.file_path"))
    .withColumn("bronze_ingested_at", current_timestamp())
)

(
    df.writeStream.format("delta")
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint)
    .outputMode("append")
    .trigger(availableNow=True)
    .toTable(target)
    .awaitTermination()
)

display(spark.table(target))

steps.title: Silver: dimensions and fact
steps.tip: Mask in silver: analysts need patterns, not names or ID numbers.
steps.tip_ar: أخفِ البيانات في Silver؛ المحللون يحتاجون الأنماط لا الأسماء ولا أرقام الهوية.

segs.t: Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) requires data minimisation and protection of personal data, and SAMA expects banks to restrict access to customer data. Analysts do not need names or ID numbers to measure re-delinquency. Silver therefore stores only the last 4 digits of the National ID / Iqama and the initials of each name. In production, also consider Unity Catalog column masks and a salted hash kept in a secret scope.
columns. SAMA reporting and the core system may use Hijri dates; add an optional Hijri column for display (action 5), never as the join or window key.

# Silver: banking.bronze.cbs_customer -> banking.silver.dim_customer (masked, MERGE)
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, concat, lit, substring, upper, trim, to_date, current_timestamp
from delta.tables import DeltaTable

base       = "abfss://data@<storage-account>.dfs.core.windows.net"
source     = "banking.bronze.cbs_customer"
target     = "banking.silver.dim_customer"
checkpoint = f"{base}/checkpoints/silver/dim_customer/"
key        = "customer_id"

def transform(df):
    return (
        df.dropDuplicates([key])
        .withColumn("dob", to_date("dob"))
        .withColumn("gender", upper(trim(col("gender"))))
        # PII masking (PDPL / SAMA): keep last 4 digits and initials only
        .withColumn("national_id_or_iqama",
                    concat(lit("******"), substring(col("national_id_or_iqama").cast("string"), -4, 4)))
        .withColumn("first_name", concat(substring("first_name", 1, 1), lit("***")))
        .withColumn("last_name",  concat(substring("last_name", 1, 1), lit("***")))
        .withColumn("load_timestamp", current_timestamp())
        .drop("source_file", "bronze_ingested_at")
    )

# Create the empty target once, with the right schema. mode("ignore") does nothing if it already exists,
# so a later run can never overwrite the dimension.
transform(spark.read.table(source).limit(0)).write.format("delta").mode("ignore").saveAsTable(target)

def upsert(batch_df, batch_id):
    s = batch_df.sparkSession            # use the batch's session (required on serverless)
    (DeltaTable.forName(s, target).alias("t")
        .merge(transform(batch_df).alias("s"), f"t.{key} = s.{key}")
        .whenMatchedUpdateAll()
        .whenNotMatchedInsertAll()
        .execute())

(
    spark.readStream.table(source)
    .writeStream
    .foreachBatch(upsert)
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint)
    .trigger(availableNow=True)
    .start()
    .awaitTermination()
)

display(spark.table(target))

# Silver: banking.bronze.cbs_repayment + dims -> banking.silver.fact_repayment (MERGE on event_id)
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, to_date, date_format, current_timestamp
from delta.tables import DeltaTable

base       = "abfss://data@<storage-account>.dfs.core.windows.net"
source     = "banking.bronze.cbs_repayment"
target     = "banking.silver.fact_repayment"
checkpoint = f"{base}/checkpoints/silver/fact_repayment/"
key        = "event_id"

def transform(df, s):
    # Current dimensions (batch read: we need the full dim, not only new rows)
    customers = s.read.table("banking.silver.dim_customer").select(
        "customer_id", "gender", col("city").alias("customer_city"),
        "customer_segment", "nationality_type")
    branches = s.read.table("banking.silver.dim_branch").select(
        "branch_id", "branch_name", col("city").alias("branch_city"), "region")
    products = s.read.table("banking.silver.dim_product").select(
        "product_code", "product_desc", "product_type", "shariah_structure")

    return (
        df.dropDuplicates([key])
        .withColumn("due_date", to_date("due_date"))
        .withColumn("cure_date", to_date("cure_date"))
        .withColumn("days_past_due", col("days_past_due").cast("int"))
        .withColumn("installment_amount_sar", col("installment_amount_sar").cast("decimal(18,2)"))
        .withColumn("outstanding_balance_sar", col("outstanding_balance_sar").cast("decimal(18,2)"))
        .withColumn("due_month", date_format("due_date", "yyyy-MM"))
        .join(customers, "customer_id", "left")
        .join(branches,  "branch_id",   "left")
        .join(products,  "product_code", "left")
        .withColumn("load_timestamp", current_timestamp())
        .drop("source_file", "bronze_ingested_at")
    )

# Create the empty target once (no-op if it exists), so a later run can never overwrite the fact
transform(spark.read.table(source).limit(0), spark).write.format("delta").mode("ignore").saveAsTable(target)

def upsert(batch_df, batch_id):
    s = batch_df.sparkSession            # use the batch's session (required on serverless)
    (DeltaTable.forName(s, target).alias("t")
        .merge(transform(batch_df, s).alias("s"), f"t.{key} = s.{key}")
        .whenMatchedUpdateAll()
        .whenNotMatchedInsertAll()
        .execute())

(
    spark.readStream.table(source)
    .writeStream
    .foreachBatch(upsert)
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint)
    .trigger(availableNow=True)
    .start()
    .awaitTermination()
)

display(spark.table(target).orderBy("event_id"))

# Gold: banking.silver.fact_repayment -> banking.gold.fact_redelinquency_event + banking.gold.agg_redelinquency_branch_product
from pyspark.sql.functions import (col, lag, datediff, when, count, sum as _sum, avg,
                                   round as _round, current_timestamp)
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

fact = spark.read.table("banking.silver.fact_repayment")   # batch read: window + lag need the full history

# Same customer, same product, in due-date order
w = Window.partitionBy("customer_id", "product_code").orderBy("due_date")

events = (
    fact
    .withColumn("prev_cure_date", lag("cure_date").over(w))
    .withColumn("days_since_last_cure", datediff(col("due_date"), col("prev_cure_date")))
    .withColumn(
        "redelinquency_30d_flag",
        when(col("days_since_last_cure").between(0, 30), 1).otherwise(0)
    )
)

# Event-level table (needed for month-over-month trends and Genie)
(events.withColumn("gold_load_timestamp", current_timestamp())
    .write.mode("overwrite").option("overwriteSchema", "true")
    .saveAsTable("banking.gold.fact_redelinquency_event"))

# KPI table: grain = branch x product
kpi = (
    events.groupBy("branch_id", "branch_name", "region",
                   "product_code", "product_desc", "product_type", "shariah_structure")
    .agg(
        count("*").alias("total_events"),
        _sum("redelinquency_30d_flag").alias("total_redelinquencies"),
        _round(_sum("redelinquency_30d_flag") / count("*") * 100, 2).alias("redelinquency_rate"),
        _round(_sum("installment_amount_sar"), 2).alias("total_amount_sar"),
        _round(avg("installment_amount_sar"), 2).alias("avg_amount_sar"),
    )
    .withColumn("gold_load_timestamp", current_timestamp())
)

(kpi.write.mode("overwrite").option("overwriteSchema", "true")
    .saveAsTable("banking.gold.agg_redelinquency_branch_product"))

display(kpi.orderBy(col("redelinquency_rate").desc()))

segs.t: brings the previous event's cure date onto the current row.
counts days from cure to the next missed installment.
0–30 days = re-delinquent (flag 1). A first event, or one after an open (uncured) event, has a null gap and gets 0.
is a percentage. Amounts are installment amounts in SAR.

SELECT branch_id, branch_name, region,
       SUM(total_events)          AS events,
       SUM(total_redelinquencies) AS redelinquencies,
       ROUND(SUM(total_redelinquencies) * 100.0 / SUM(total_events), 2) AS rate_pct
FROM banking.gold.agg_redelinquency_branch_product
GROUP BY branch_id, branch_name, region
ORDER BY rate_pct DESC, redelinquencies DESC
LIMIT 5;
-- top row: BR004 Jeddah Tahlia, Makkah region, 3 events, 2 re-delinquencies, 66.67%

segs.t: Q2. Which product drives most re-delinquencies?

SELECT product_type, product_code, product_desc,
       SUM(total_redelinquencies) AS redelinquencies,
       ROUND(SUM(total_redelinquencies) * 100.0
             / SUM(SUM(total_redelinquencies)) OVER (), 2) AS share_of_all_pct
FROM banking.gold.agg_redelinquency_branch_product
GROUP BY product_type, product_code, product_desc
HAVING SUM(total_redelinquencies) > 0
ORDER BY redelinquencies DESC, product_code;
-- PF02 and CC02 lead with 2 each (25% each); by product_type, Credit Card = 4 of 8 (50%)

WITH m AS (
  SELECT due_month,
         COUNT(*)                    AS events,
         SUM(redelinquency_30d_flag) AS redelinquencies
  FROM banking.gold.fact_redelinquency_event
  GROUP BY due_month
)
SELECT due_month, events, redelinquencies,
       ROUND(redelinquencies * 100.0 / events, 2)          AS rate_pct,
       redelinquencies - LAG(redelinquencies) OVER (ORDER BY due_month) AS mom_change
FROM m
ORDER BY due_month;
-- 2026-06: 6 / 0 | 2026-07: 8 / 3 | 2026-08: 7 / 3 | 2026-09: 7 / 2 | 2026-10: 2 / 0

intro_sections.title: The story
intro_sections.lead: Najd National Bank (fictional) runs personal finance, auto finance, credit cards and home finance (Murabaha, Tawarruq, Ijara) through branches from Riyadh and Jeddah to Abha and Tabuk.
intro_sections.text: When a customer misses an installment, collections chase them until they are current again, and count it as a win. But many cured customers miss again within a month. Each repeat raises IFRS 9 expected credit losses and provisions, sends the same customers back to the same collectors, and draws SAMA questions the bank cannot answer today.
intro_sections.quote: Which products, segments and branches keep sending customers back into arrears?
intro_sections.tip: This guide follows the 16 steps of a reference end-to-end Databricks project, in the same order and with the same tools.

side.title: What counts as re-delinquent?
side.caption: A new missed installment due 0–30 days after the same customer cured the previous one on the same product.

cards.title: From an empty repo
cards.text: You begin with nothing but a GitHub repo. Every resource, notebook and file is created along the way.

cards.title: One step, one commit
cards.text: Each step adds only its own files and ends with a commit, so your history tells the story of the build.

cards.title: Built for a bank
cards.text: Data residency, Unity Catalog governance and PDPL masking are part of the build, not an afterthought.

items.name: Staging
items.text: Raw CSV feeds in ADLS Gen2, where a nightly core-banking extract would drop them.

items.name: Bronze
items.text: Auto Loader ingests each feed incrementally, as-is, into banking.bronze.

items.name: Silver
items.text: De-duplicated, PDPL-masked data MERGEd into three dimensions and one wide repayment fact.

items.name: Gold
items.text: The 30-day re-delinquency flag and a branch × product KPI table.

items.name: Serving
items.text: A Genie space for plain-English questions and an AI/BI dashboard in Databricks One.

items.text: A Lakeflow Job, a Databricks Asset Bundle and GitHub Actions CI/CD from dev to prod.
